(a) A certificate of number granted under this Act shall be pocket size, shall be at all times available for inspection on the vessel for which issued when the vessel is in use, and may not be valid for more than three years. The certificate of number for vessels less than twenty-six feet in length and leased or rented to another for the latter’s noncommercial use of less than twenty-four hours may be retained on shore by the vessel’s owner or his representative at the place from which the vessel departs or returns to the possession of the owner or his representative. A vessel which does not have the certificate of number on board shall be identified while in use, and comply with such other requirements, as the issuing authority prescribes. 
    (b) The owner of a vessel numbered under this Act shall furnish to the issuing authority notice of the transfer of all or part of his interest in the vessel, or of the destruction or abandonment of the vessel, within a reasonable time thereof, and shall furnish notice of any change of address within a reasonable time of the change, in accordance with prescribed regulations.

fable.w: The section sets requirements for vessel certificates of number and obliges owners to notify the issuing authority of transfers, destruction, or address changes. That is a compliance duty on private parties, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. The tempting reading is that "prescribed regulations" and "as the issuing authority prescribes" signal rulemaking, but these are passing references to requirements set elsewhere rather than a grant of rulemaking authority, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, or a right to sue.
fable.s: shall furnish notice of any change of address within a reasonable time of the change, in accordance with prescribed regulations

qwen_block.w: This section imposes administrative reporting requirements on vessel owners regarding transfers, destruction, or address changes. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The interaction is purely regulatory compliance, not participatory governance.
qwen_block.s: The owner of a vessel numbered under this Act shall furnish to the issuing authority notice of the transfer of all or part of his interest in the vessel, or of the destruction or abandonment of the vessel, within a reasonable time thereof, and shall furnish notice of any change of address within a reasonable time of the change, in accordance with prescribed regulations.

opus.w: The section relies on regulations: owners must give notice "in accordance with prescribed regulations," and vessel requirements are set "as the issuing authority prescribes." Under the definition and Example 6, requiring or authorizing rulemaking counts as participation because rulemaking brings in public comment. The tempting "No" reading treats the owner's notices as mere compliance, which on its own would not be participation. But the dependence on rulemaking makes this a Yes.
opus.s: shall furnish notice of any change of address within a reasonable time of the change, in accordance with prescribed regulations
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "No": this section reads like plain administrative rules about carrying a certificate on board and notifying the issuing authority of changes. The notices owners must send look like compliance duties, not a say in a federal decision. But the DEFINITION counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation, and Example 6 counts even optional authority to regulate. Here the requirements are set "as the issuing authority prescribes" and owners must give notice "in accordance with prescribed regulations." So the section depends on rulemaking. One weakness: the issuing authority may be a state rather than a federal agency, and the reference to regulations is indirect, so my confidence is moderate.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes administrative reporting obligations on vessel owners regarding transfers, destruction, or address changes. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from outside parties before making a decision. The communication is one-way (owner to government) for record-keeping purposes, which does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The owner of a vessel numbered under this Act shall furnish to the issuing authority notice of the transfer of all or part of his interest in the vessel, or of the destruction or abandonment of the vessel, within a reasonable time thereof, and shall furnish notice of any change of address within a reasonable time of the change, in accordance with prescribed regulations.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for vessel owners to furnish notice of transfer or address changes constitutes "participation" because it involves communication from an outside party (the owner) to the government. However, this is merely an administrative reporting requirement for record-keeping and regulatory compliance, not a consultation or coordination process where the government seeks input from outsiders before making a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications and administrative filings that do not involve the government consulting with outsiders to inform a decision.
